title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #13

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Stem
   B. Roots
   C. Seed coat
   D. Flower

2. How do most flowering plants make new plants? (1 mark)
   A. By seeds
   B. By giving birth
   C. By laying eggs
   D. By walking away

3. In which part do you find the seeds of a mango? (1 mark)
   A. Stem
   B. Fruit
   C. Leaf
   D. Root

4. Which of these gives the young plant its first food before its leaves open? (1 mark)
   A. The bark
   B. The wind
   C. The flower
   D. The seed

5. What happens to a dead plant? (1 mark)
   A. It turns into an animal
   B. It flies away
   C. It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   D. It becomes a rock

6. A student says a tree is not alive because it does not move from place to place. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Plants show life by growing and responding
   B. Trees are not plants
   C. Trees are made of stone
   D. Only animals grow

7. A tadpole grows into a frog. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Only fish grow
   B. Tadpoles are plants
   C. Animals do not grow
   D. Animals grow and change

8. Which of these is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Spider
   C. Snail
   D. Ant

9. Which of these is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Frog
   C. Snake
   D. Earthworm

10. Which of these animals is a reptile? (1 mark)
   A. Tilapia
   B. Butterfly
   C. Hen
   D. Lizard

11. Which of these do we drink to keep digestion healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Clean safe water
   C. Sugary drinks all the time
   D. Muddy water

12. The stomach is described in the lesson as being like (1 mark)
   A. A sharp knife
   B. A hard stone
   C. A stretchy bag
   D. A long ladder

13. What are the symptoms of worms mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Fast running
   B. Loud voice
   C. Clear skin
   D. Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness

14. Which activity shows that air takes up space? (1 mark)
   A. Blowing up a balloon
   B. Lighting a candle
   C. Singing a song
   D. Shining a torch

15. How many grams are in 5 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5000
   B. 500
   C. 50 000
   D. 50

16. An empty bottle is full of (1 mark)
   A. Air
   B. Sand
   C. Nothing
   D. Water

17. Which state of matter has its own shape and fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Liquid
   C. Steam only
   D. Solid

18. Which are the three states of matter? (1 mark)
   A. Solid, liquid and gas
   B. Hard, soft and rough
   C. Big, medium and small
   D. Hot, warm and cold

19. Which is the best order of managing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throw, burn, bury
   B. Recycle, reuse, reduce
   C. Burn, bury, throw
   D. Reduce, reuse, recycle

20. Why must we conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Water is not needed
   B. Water is always free
   C. Fresh water is limited
   D. Water never ends

21. Why do people spread ash or sand on a slippery path? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavy
   B. To reduce friction
   C. To increase friction
   D. To make it hot

22. Which of these can change the shape of dough? (1 mark)
   A. Looking at it
   B. Talking to it
   C. Pressing with a force
   D. Leaving it alone

23. What effect of force is shown when a goalkeeper stops a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Changes its colour
   B. Starts a moving object
   C. Stops a moving object
   D. Makes it lighter

24. Why are tyres made with rough patterns? (1 mark)
   A. To reduce friction
   B. To make them lighter
   C. To grip the road
   D. To make them shiny

25. How does light travel? (1 mark)
   A. In curves only
   B. In zigzags
   C. In circles
   D. In straight lines

26. Which of these is transparent? (1 mark)
   A. Wood
   B. Clear glass
   C. Thick cardboard
   D. Metal

27. You want to see if a material is opaque. What do you do? (1 mark)
   A. Weigh it
   B. Smell it
   C. Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   D. Taste it

28. Which use of heat helps us on a cold morning? (1 mark)
   A. Making sound
   B. Growing shadows
   C. Keeping us warm
   D. Making things dark

29. Why is cooking food useful? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food cold
   B. It makes food soft and safer to eat
   C. It makes food dirty
   D. It makes food raw

30. Which use of heat makes cloth smooth? (1 mark)
   A. Making shadows
   B. Playing music
   C. Reading a book
   D. Ironing clothes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how rainwater can be harvested from a school roof. (3 marks)

32. Name the three Rs of waste management. (2 marks)

33. Explain why steam from a kettle is invisible although we see a white cloud above the spout. Say what state of matter the cloud is. (5 marks)

34. Describe how you can show that a liquid takes the shape of its container. (3 marks)

35. Describe how a bean seed grows into a young plant. (3 marks)

36. List four signs of life in plants. (2 marks)

37. State two functions of roots. (2 marks)

38. Name two invertebrates that are found near your school. (2 marks)

39. Define matter and give two examples. (2 marks)

40. State two reasons for conserving water. (2 marks)

41. What is evaporation? Give one example. (2 marks)

42. Describe two properties of a liquid. (3 marks)

43. Explain the importance of heat in daily life. (5 marks)

44. Explain why the flat paper and stone dropped together do not land at the same time. (3 marks)

45. What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate? (2 marks)

46. Plan a project to sensitise your community about the importance of water conservation. State the steps. (5 marks)

47. Describe how windows, roofs and walls can be used to make a house brighter by day. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Roots
   Roots take in water and mineral salts.

2. A — By seeds
   Most flowering plants reproduce by making seeds inside fruits.

3. B — Fruit
   Seeds are found inside fruits.

4. D — The seed
   The seed contains stored food that feeds the young plant at first.

5. C — It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   Dead plants decay and give nutrients back to the soil.

6. A — Plants show life by growing and responding
   Plants show many signs of life even though they do not walk.

7. D — Animals grow and change
   Young animals grow and may change shape as they become adults.

8. A — Hen
   A hen is a bird and has a backbone.

9. D — Earthworm
   An earthworm has a soft body and no backbone.

10. D — Lizard
   A lizard has dry scaly skin.

11. B — Clean safe water
   Clean safe water helps digestion and prevents disease.

12. C — A stretchy bag
   The stomach is a stretchy bag that churns food.

13. D — Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   These are signs that worms may be present.

14. A — Blowing up a balloon
   The balloon swells because air takes up space inside.

15. A — 5000
   5 x 1000 = 5000 g.

16. A — Air
   An empty bottle contains air.

17. D — Solid
   Solids keep their shape and volume.

18. A — Solid, liquid and gas
   Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.

19. D — Reduce, reuse, recycle
   First make less waste, then reuse, then recycle.

20. C — Fresh water is limited
   Only a small part of the world's water is fresh and usable.

21. C — To increase friction
   Rough material improves grip.

22. C — Pressing with a force
   A force can squeeze and stretch dough.

23. C — Stops a moving object
   The force of the hands stops the ball.

24. C — To grip the road
   Grip needs friction.

25. D — In straight lines
   Light travels in straight lines.

26. B — Clear glass
   Clear glass lets light through.

27. C — Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   If no light passes, it is opaque.

28. C — Keeping us warm
   Heat keeps our bodies warm.

29. B — It makes food soft and safer to eat
   Heat kills many germs.

30. D — Ironing clothes
   A hot iron flattens cloth.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter. The gutter leads to a pipe which fills a covered tank.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for roof and gutter, 1 mark for pipe, 1 mark for tank.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Steam is water as a gas and it is invisible. The white cloud is made of tiny water drops which are liquid.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for steam is a gas, 1 mark for invisible, 1 mark for white cloud being tiny drops, 1 mark for liquid, 1 mark for a clear explanation.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 200 ml of water into a tall glass and then into a wide bowl. The shape of the water changes but the amount stays the same.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two containers, 1 mark for shape changing, 1 mark for the volume the same.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: The seed takes in water and a root comes out first and goes down. Then a shoot grows up and opens into leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and seed, 1 mark for root first, 1 mark for shoot and leaves.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes, die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four correct signs.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: They hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Some store food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two correct examples such as ant, earthworm, snail, butterfly, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct invertebrate.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Examples: water, stone, air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for two examples.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: To have enough water for all, to save money, for crops and animals, to protect sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Liquid water turning into water vapour, for example wet clothes drying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for an example.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A liquid has a fixed volume and no shape of its own. It takes the shape of its container and can be poured.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of two properties and 1 mark for the example.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Heat keeps us warm, cooks food, dries clothes and crops, helps plants grow, makes rain by evaporation, and is used to make metals and glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity pulls both down but air pushes up on the flat paper more, so it falls slowly. The stone is little affected by the air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for gravity on both, 1 mark for air pushing paper, 1 mark for stone landing first.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A vertebrate has a backbone and an invertebrate has no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a message, make posters, put them near taps and gates, speak at assembly, do a demonstration of saving water and check results.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Large windows let in light, translucent roof sheets let in light, light-coloured walls reflect light, open curtains.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.
